hook: A slow loaded freight train and a fast baseball are both hard to stop, for different reasons: one has enormous mass, the other a large speed. Momentum combines the two into one vector quantity, and it turns out to be the quantity collisions and explosions cannot change.

options: a vector with size and direction
prereq.why: Velocity has a direction, carried by its sign in one dimension.

prereq.q: The center of mass of a system is
Forces between objects inside a system are
prereq.why: Forces between parts of the system are internal; Newton's third law makes them cancel in pairs.

figure.caption: Two carts with equal momentum: one heavy and slow, one light and fast, with different kinetic energies.

chain.cause: An object of mass m moves with velocity v
chain.effect: it has momentum p = mv, a vector along v, in kg·m/s
the system's momentum is the vector sum, and momenta in opposite directions cancel

chain.cause: The system's momentum is divided by its total mass
chain.effect: the result is the velocity of the center of mass, v_cm = Σp/Σm

chain.cause: Objects push on each other briefly and hard (a collision or explosion)
chain.effect: the internal forces dominate, so the system's momentum is the same just before and just after

ideas: Momentum p = mv is a vector in the direction of the velocity, in kg·m/s.
A system's momentum is the vector sum of its parts. Opposite momenta cancel; kinetic energies never do.
Same momentum does not mean same kinetic energy: K = p²/(2m), so the lighter object has more K.
The velocity of the center of mass is v_cm = Σp/Σm.

The collision model: forces between colliding objects are internal and much larger than outside forces, so the system's momentum is the same just before and just after. An explosion is the same model in reverse.

misconception.wrong: A heavy truck always has more momentum than a light ball.
misconception.right: Momentum is mass times velocity. A fast, light object can have as much momentum as a slow, heavy one, and two momenta in opposite directions can cancel.

summary: Momentum p = mv is a vector along the velocity. A system's momentum is the vector sum of its parts, and its center of mass moves at v_cm = Σp/Σm. In collisions and explosions the internal forces dominate, so the momentum just before equals the momentum just after.
